BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary point – the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" is disregarded.** The note asserts that clauses tagged [STANDARD] have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that the disclosure framework and limitation package are "already accepted". Under playbook §0.4/6.3, counterparty labels do not establish agreement; nothing in our authority process records any such clearance, and no written authority from Amelia Frost exists for any fallback. Every clause below is reviewed in full against our playbook. Note also that the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (¶11) contradicts the note by stating "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included".

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The Seller's number happens to match our conditional fallback, but no Amelia Frost written authority identifying this draft exists, so the fallback is not available.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the "excess only" mechanic would permanently forfeit AUD 250,000 of loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a default rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: 24 months; limitations apply only where expressly stated to a category.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost approval (none given), and the default rule is a hidden override of the separate regimes.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap recovery on title to the very shares being bought at 20% of price.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: no carve-out; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature".
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Insist on a full carve-out as a non-negotiable.** This is a no-waiver item under our playbook and the Seller's drafting would purport to limit liability for the Seller's own fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Schedule 7; DL ¶1.1–1.2).
- Buyer wants: only specific, fair disclosure of matters set out in the Disclosure Letter, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
- Recommendation: **Reject whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure; require a specific fair-disclosure standard.** General disclosure of ~11 data room items would effectively disclose against every warranty without identifying what is being disclosed.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete the blanket exclusion; any residual qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals, mirrored by named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3.** A "discoverable" standard converts the Buyer's diligence into the Seller's defence and duplicates the already-rejected general disclosure mechanism.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL ¶2 confirms no final consent and no evidence of cl 11.3 conditions being satisfied.
- Buyer wants: condition precedent requiring effective consent under cl 11.2 AND evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not satisfied by mere delivery of a letter.
- Recommendation: **Reject; redraft as a hard CP with condition-satisfaction evidence.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue and reasonable endeavours plus a deemed-satisfaction mechanic gives no protection on a material customer.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL ¶3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion; any post-completion release only with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release; require payout and releases at Completion.** A debt-free/cash-free deal cannot complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and unreleased security still in place.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL ¶5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs either as a specific funds-flow line item paid from Seller proceeds or expressly Seller-funded; on-costs quantified.
- Recommendation: **Require a specific line item (or Seller indemnity) covering bonuses plus on-costs.** "A matter for the Seller" is not a contractual obligation and the liability crystallises in the Company at Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL ¶4: DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- Buyer wants: broader indemnity covering all loss arising from non-transfer or defective title to SOW3 Project Materials (and any other Ironquay deliverables), with the SOW3 payment/cure mechanism preserved; independent verification of the AUD 180,000 status either way.
- Recommendation: **Broaden the indemnity and require pre-Completion evidence of payment and assignment.** The AUD 180,000 figure is unverified in both directions, and a payment-only indemnity does not address loss if the IP never transfers.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL ¶6: ~1,240 records, unknown access/scope, notification question open, no loss figure.
- Buyer wants: covenant to preserve logs, complete investigation, provide updates before Completion; specific indemnity or warranty protection for consequences; no assumption of confirmed breach or of no breach.
- Recommendation: **Require preservation/investigation/update covenants and keep the matter open; do not accept the "not material" characterisation.** The facts are genuinely undetermined, so neither side should price or dismiss it yet.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. DL ¶8: three renewals of AUD 110,000 (DD-008, DD-011); silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: information on timing, terminability and whether any amount is accrued or committed as at Completion; treatment decided on facts.
- Recommendation: **Assess, do not accept the characterisation; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** The disclosure itself admits it does not establish ordinary-course status.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: single general regime applied to "all Claims of any nature", with Tax/IP "settled under the general regime" and title folded in.
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment/leakage and covenant claims as distinct categories with their own caps, periods and thresholds; no default rule that general limitations apply across categories.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insist on express category separation.** The Seller's "unless expressly stated otherwise" and "all Claims" language is a hidden general-regime override.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL ¶10 concedes this is the source relied on and does not state Buyer verification is complete.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC search, constitution, share certificates, board/member resolutions, encumbrance (PPSR) searches, Seller capacity and authority documents, and unencumbered-title/full-authority warranties under the Fundamental regime.
- Recommendation: **Require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence before Completion.** DD-012 is an internal document supplied by the Seller and is not independent proof of ownership.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: "settled under the general regime above".
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP terms remain OPEN pending separate negotiation of specific indemnity, cap and period; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed.
- Recommendation: **Reject the "settled" assertion; record Tax/IP as open.** A unilateral statement that terms are settled does not make them so, and our playbook treats these as unresolved.

---

**Summary for the deal team:** None of the sixteen positions is acceptable as drafted. Four are structural (fraud carve-out, fundamental/title regime, category separation, disclosure scope) and should be treated as deal-conditioning. Three require pre-Completion deliverables rather than drafting changes (Bluefen consent evidence, Riverlark payout/releases, independent title evidence). The cap (20%) and claims period (18 months) match our fallbacks numerically but **no Amelia Frost authority has been given**, so our response must counter at 25% / 24 months. Recommend that the reply to Seller's counsel also expressly rejects the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" characterisation of any clause as cleared or agreed.
